title: Stage A: the assisted loop (tasks.py next -> contract -> do -> check -> evidence)
behavior: A goal runner for the assisted loop (docs/harness.md 12 Stage A). scripts/loop.py keeps an append-only state file (tasks/loop.jsonl: runs, rounds, interventions) and decides each next step from the task file, never from the model's say-so: 'begin' opens a run (max 5 rounds, --bridge widens the pool like tasks.py next; lists the parked author questions first), 'next' opens a round on tasks.py next's pick or names the one action the round's task needs by its state (write the contract, do the work via the area's agent, spawn forest-checker, release + in-game evidence, deploy-watch, evidence to confirm, end the round), 'end' closes a round with a required one-paragraph summary and an outcome read from the task's status (an in-progress task is refused: pass or park first), 'intervene' logs a human fix, 'report' prints the run (rounds, passes, parked, interventions, summaries). Stop conditions are machine checks in 'next': 5 rounds done, nothing left in the pool, 3 rounds in a row with no progress; a task given a third checker revise in its round is parked automatically (needs author-decision, the faults as the question) and the loop moves on. tasks.py stats gains the loop line. A work-loop skill holds the procedure (main orchestrates; each task's work goes to a fresh subagent by area, tiny docs / harness edits main does itself; one summary per round), and workflow.md / decisions.md / the session-switching memory carry the exception to one session, one task.

title: Bot settings page on /admin
behavior: The design in docs/knowledge-bot.md *Bot settings page on /admin* (agreed 2026-10-05): an owner-only 'Bot' tab on the site's /admin behind the existing admin token sets the bot's answer channels (by name, checkboxes, from the channel list the bot posts to the site), DMs on/off, per-user limits per hour / per day, model order (the FOREST_BOT_MODELS string), thinking level, research-queue channel. The bot polls the site about once a minute with its own bot-only token in its own header, applies the settings live (no restart) and caches the last good settings in its data dir; on a failed fetch or no settings stored it keeps the last good / the .env values. The tab shows what the bot runs: 'applied hh:mm, bot vX' from the bot's last poll.
scope: site/ (endpoints, store, /admin tab, tests), bot/ForestBot (settings poller, BotConfig live reload, channel list report, tests), docs/knowledge-bot.md section from planned to built, docs/website.md / docs/areas/site.md / bot/README.md lines for the new env var(s); the VPS .env change for the shared bot token is a ship step for main

title: HUD profiles carry their reference resolution (UiScale), so a profile made at another resolution applies scaled
behavior: A HUD profile file records the reference resolution its positions and sizes were saved at (@HUD.ReferenceWidth / @HUD.ReferenceHeight). Applying one whose reference differs from the install's converts its places (HUD column, free values, splits and results panels: x by width ratio, y by height ratio; negative sentinels kept) and pixel sizes (splits / results widths: height ratio) into the install's reference, so every piece sits and sizes the same relative to the screen. A profile without the keys (every existing file) applies unchanged. Text size, value scale and row counts are relative already and are not converted.
scope: ui-redesign: src/Data (pure conversion + tests), src/Core/HudWidgets.Profiles.cs, the RegisterProfileEntry calls in HudSettings.cs / PracticeRunModule.Splits.cs / .Results.cs; one log line when a profile is converted (+ log-lines.md)

notes: tasks/notes/T-0360.md Author 2026-10-15: clarity matters for good UI. Since T-0324 (v0.24.300) the window draws under GUI.matrix x Screen.height/768, so IMGUI rasterises glyphs at the 768p size and stretches them (soft at 1080p+). Traps (gotcha 112): groups / scroll views clip BEFORE the matrix, so CrispText's enlarge-inside-1/k trick is cut at 1/k of its width in the window (hence CrispText.Plain); GUIToScreenPoint leaves offsets unscaled (UiKit.Unclip). Candidate ways (needs research + a choice): draw the window at scale 1 with every size x k (fonts, rects, paddings - all layout constants); or route every control through UiKit wrappers that draw text crisp and fix the clip; or another IMGUI route. Compare shots against tasks/notes/shots/2026-10-15-t0324-1080-*.
